newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise in sluggish trade.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Monday in quiet trading as investors remained sidelined due to political uncertainty, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.81 percent, or 1.51 points, to 187.44 on low turnover of 46 million shekels against 40 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 index gained 0.80 percent to 197.78.

"The market is rising but on very low volume and it looks very bad. Most investors are sitting on the fence waiting to see what will happen with the peace process," said Yoram Ben-Ya'ir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators resumed talks on Sunday following last week's White House summit, which was called after clashes in the West Bank and Gaza that killed 74 people.

"All investors are in a holding pattern and activity is minimal. Today's turnover is simply ridiculous and there's simply nothing much to say about such a market," said a trader at Lehava Investments.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 0.50 percent to 143,518 on volume of 3.4 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 0.25 percent to 28,520 on volume of 2.9 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 1.25 percent to 786 on turnover of 2.1 million shekels.
